title: Etale section spaces along finite locally free scheme maps
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $p:Z\to U$ be a finite locally free morphism of $S$-schemes [def-pc-finite-locally-free], with possibly variable rank and rank zero. Let $W$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and $q:W\to Z$ a representable etale morphism, with schemes regarded as algebraic spaces by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space, def-weil-etale-morphism]. For every $U$-scheme $V$ put $Z_V=Z\times_UV$ and $W_V=W\times_UV$ [def-pc-fibre-product, lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The functor
$$V\longmapsto\{\sigma:Z_V\to W_V\mid q_V\circ\sigma=\operatorname{id}_{Z_V}\}$$
with restriction by base change is represented by an algebraic space $E$ over $U$, and $E\to U$ is etale. In particular, on etale scheme charts of $E$, the maps to $U$ are etale. No separatedness or quasi-compactness hypothesis on $q$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 05XR, lemma-space-of-sections; includes the nonseparated case in the second proof paragraph.

proof.text: First, representability of $q$ and the identity scheme test $Z\to Z$ identify $W=W\times_ZZ$ with a scheme; its representing maps are the actual sheaf maps. Write $F$ for the displayed section functor. It is an fppf sheaf: for an fppf covering $\{T_i\to T\}$ the schemes $Z_{T_i}$ cover $Z_T$ by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change]. View a section as a map $a:Z_T\to W$ satisfying $qa=\operatorname{pr}_Z$; its map to $W_T$ is $(a,\operatorname{pr}_T)$. The sheaf axiom for $W$ glues compatible $a_i$ uniquely, and that for $Z$ verifies the displayed equation after gluing. Thus the glued map is again a section. Under any scheme base change, $Z_T\to T$ remains finite, flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence, lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence].

source.place: Tag 05XR, lemma-space-of-sections, sheaf condition and base-change setup

proof.text: Suppose for now that $q:W\to Z$ is separated. Finite maps are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], so $p$ is separated and locally of finite type. Etale maps are locally of finite presentation, hence locally of finite type. Composition permanence [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] shows that $W\to U$ is separated and locally of finite type. Therefore [lem-sfb-unmarked-finite-open-parts-space] supplies an algebraic space $P=(W/U)_{fin}$ chartwise etale over $U$, with $P(T)$ the open subschemes $D\subset W_T$ finite over $T$. For a section $\sigma:Z_T\to W_T$, the equality $q_T\sigma=1$ makes $\sigma$ a monomorphism. It is etale by cancellation [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]; hence it is an open immersion by [lem-sfb-space-etale-monomorphism-open]. Its image $D_\sigma$ is isomorphic to $Z_T$, so is finite over $T$. This gives $F\to P$, naturally in $T$. It is injective: on a specified $D$, the section must be the inverse of $q_T|_D$.

source.place: Tag 05XR, lemma-space-of-sections, first proof paragraph: section image and finite-part functor

proof.text: For a test $T\to P$, let $D\subset W_T$ be its finite open subscheme. The map $D\to Z_T$ is etale: it is the composite of an open immersion with the base change of $q$, using [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation, lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]. Consequently $D\to T$ is flat and locally of finite presentation, by [lem-pc-flat-compose, lem-sbc-locally-finite-presentation-composition] applied to $D\to Z_T\to T$. It is universally closed because it is finite [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. The target $Z_T\to T$ is finite, hence locally of finite type, closed and separated. All six hypotheses of [lem-sfb-universal-isomorphism-open] now apply to $D\to Z_T$ over $T$. Obtain an open $T^\circ\subset T$ such that $B\to T$ factors through $T^\circ$ exactly when $D_B\to Z_B$ is an isomorphism. Such an isomorphism gives the unique section with image $D_B$ by inversion; conversely a section with that image gives precisely this isomorphism. These inverse operations commute with pullback. Hence $T\times_PF=h_{T^\circ}$, including its projection to $T$.

source.place: Tag 05XR, lemma-space-of-sections, first proof paragraph: open universal isomorphism locus

proof.text: The preceding scheme tests show that $F\to P$ is representable by open immersions. By [lem-sfb-presheaf-space-target-bootstrap], $F$ is an algebraic space. By [lem-a1-space-open-chart-tests] its map to $P$ is chartwise etale; composition with $P\to U$ is chartwise etale by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. This proves the separated case over every scheme base, with variable finite locally free rank allowed. No uniform basis, constant degree or nonempty fibre was used.

source.place: Tag 05XR, lemma-space-of-sections, end of first proof paragraph

proof.text: For general $q$, choose a representable surjective etale $r:W'\to W$ with $W'$ a disjoint union of affine schemes by [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. Both $r$ and $q'=qr$ are separated: on each affine component this follows from [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated]; on the product of two distinct components their diagonals have empty intersection, while on a same-component product the diagonal is closed. Thus the whole diagonal is closed, since those products form an open cover. Composition gives $q'$ etale. Apply the separated case of steps 2--4 to $W'\to Z\to U$ to obtain its section space $F'$ etale over $U$, with map $F'\to F$ given by postcomposition with $r$. For $(T,\sigma)\in F(T)$, put $K=W'_T\times_{W_T,\sigma}Z_T$. This is a scheme, and $K\to Z_T$ is a surjective etale separated map, by base change of $r$ [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests, lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change].

source.place: Tag 05XR, lemma-space-of-sections, second proof paragraph: separated cover; correcting W to W-prime in its separatedness sentence

proof.text: For every $B\to T$, an element of $(T\times_FF')(B)$ is a section $\tau:Z_B\to W'_B$ with $r_B\tau=\sigma_B$. Send it to $(\tau,1):Z_B\to K_B$; projection back to $W'_B$ is the inverse. Both operations are formed by the fibre-product universal property and commute with every $B'\to B$. Thus $T\times_FF'$ is the section functor of $K\to Z_T\to T$. Steps 2--4 apply because $K\to Z_T$ is separated etale and $Z_T\to T$ is finite locally free. They represent this functor by an algebraic space $F''$ chartwise etale over $T$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-etale-cover-local-sections] to the surjective etale map $K\to Z_T$ over the finite scheme $Z_T\to T$: after a surjective etale $T'\to T$ it has a section. The same applies after every base change to $T$, so $F''\to T$ is surjective and $F'\to F$ is surjective as an etale sheaf map. This verifies all scheme tests, not merely geometric fibres.

source.place: Tag 05XR, lemma-space-of-sections, second proof paragraph: explicit fibre-product functor and surjectivity

proof.text: The fppf sheaf $F$ from step 1 has the cover $F'\to F$ whose scheme-test pullbacks are the algebraic spaces $F''$ from step 6. Their maps to the tests are surjective and etale, hence flat and locally of finite presentation on scheme charts [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Therefore [lem-sfb-fppf-space-atlas-bootstrap] proves that $F$ is an algebraic space, without any assumption on its diagonal. Choose a scheme atlas $A\to F'$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Its composite $A\to F$ is representable [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. On every scheme test $T\to F$, its pullback factors as $A\times_FT\to F''\to T$; the first arrow is the base change of $A\to F'$, the second is chartwise etale. By [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence] this is etale, and it is surjective since both arrows are. Hence $A\to F$ is a representable surjective etale atlas. The composite $A\to F'\to U$ is etale. Source-atlas detection [lem-trf-space-etale-source-atlas-detection](3) now gives that $F\to U$ is chartwise etale, precisely including the asserted maps on etale scheme charts. Take $E=F$ with the natural section bijections already constructed.
